_about: Colour accents for retailers named in recall notices, keyed by the shop name of retailers.tsv.
Rule: a colour is used only when the retailer itself publishes it. None of the retailers below publishes
colour values on a brand or press page (searched 17 Nov 2026; only third-party colour sites list values, and
those are not used). What a few retailers do publish is the colour their own website declares in its code
(<meta name=theme-color>, <meta name=msapplication-TileColor>, or the web-app manifest). That declared value
is the 'accent' below, with the page it was read from, the exact tag, and the date.
Everyone else gets the neutral style (status 'not found'), with what was checked.
The accent is shown only as a colour band and a swatch next to the shop's name; text is never set on it
unless 'on_accent' reaches WCAG AA 4.5:1 against it (tests/test_retailers.py checks every pair).
Logos and trademarked marks are not used.

Lidl.note: The page's theme-color is white; the tile colour is the yellow of the logo.

Combi.note: The page's manifest declares white; the tile colour is green.

Kaufland.note: No theme or tile colour, no manifest colour, no colour on the press pages (unternehmen.kaufland.de).

Edeka.note: The site answered an automated request with a short block page; no brand-colour page found.

Rewe.note: No theme or tile colour, no manifest colour.

Globus.note: Tile colour #da532c is the default of a favicon generator, not a brand colour; theme and manifest colours are white.

Penny.note: Theme, tile and manifest colours are white.

V-Markt.note: A stylesheet variable --accent:#de9238 exists, but nothing says it is the brand colour, so it is not used.

non_supermarkets._about: Named sellers that are not food retailers: shown with their name, always in the neutral style.
